answer: Each identity needs one registered trademark: the office examines and publishes it for opposition; only a granted registration earns weight. Duplicates and lookalikes are rejected, so one mark backs one identity, every filing entering the marble register. Each fake costs 700 filing plus 500 attorney fees, 1,200 total, with a 12-month wait under falcon-eyed opposition; 100 fakes cost 120,000 units and a year. Paper marks fail fast: rivals oppose lookalikes, the office cancels marks with no sales, and no farm can grow an orchard of fake brands — each needs its own goods and customers.
